extraction.name: NWPU-RESISC45
extraction.description: NWPU-RESISC45 is a publicly available benchmark dataset for REmote Sensing Image Scene Classification (RESISC), created by Northwestern Polytechnical University (NWPU). The dataset contains 31,500 remote sensing images divided into 45 scene classes, with 700 images per class. Each image has a size of 256×256 pixels in the RGB color space. The spatial resolution varies from about 30 m to 0.2 m per pixel for most classes (except island, lake, mountain, and snowberg which have lower spatial resolutions). The 45 scene classes include: airplane, airport, baseball diamond, basketball court, beach, bridge, chaparral, church, circular farmland, cloud, commercial area, dense residential, desert, forest, freeway, golf course, ground track field, harbor, industrial area, intersection, island, lake, meadow, medium residential, mobile home park, mountain, overpass, palace, parking lot, railway, railway station, rectangular farmland, river, roundabout, runway, sea ice, ship, snowberg, sparse residential, stadium, storage tank, tennis court, terrace, thermal power station, and wetland.
extraction.creator: Northwestern Polytechnical University (NWPU)
extraction.citeAs: G. Cheng, J. Han, and X. Lu, "Remote Sensing Image Scene Classification: Benchmark and State of the Art," Proceedings of the IEEE, 2017.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was extracted, by experts in the field of remote sensing image interpretation, from Google Earth (Google Inc.), which maps the Earth by the superimposition of images obtained from satellite imagery, aerial photography, and geographic information system (GIS) onto a 3D globe. The 31,500 images cover more than 100 countries and regions all over the world, including developing, transition, and highly developed economies. Scene class selection was performed by first investigating all scene classes of existing datasets to form 30 widely-used scene categories, then searching keywords such as 'OBIA', 'GEOBIA', 'land cover classification', 'land use classification', 'geographic image retrieval', and 'geospatial object detection' on Web of Science and Google Scholar to select 15 additional meaningful scene classes, yielding 45 total scene classes.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Images extracted from Google Earth (Google Inc.), which combines satellite imagery, aerial photography, and GIS data onto a 3D globe. Images cover more than 100 countries and regions worldwide.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Images were carefully selected under all kinds of weathers, seasons, illumination conditions, imaging conditions, and scales to ensure rich variations in translation, viewpoint, object pose and appearance, spatial resolution, illumination, background, and occlusion. All images were standardized to a size of 256×256 pixels in the RGB color space.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Images were extracted and labeled by experts in the field of remote sensing image interpretation. The 45 scene classes were selected by investigating existing datasets to form 30 widely-used categories and then searching keywords on Web of Science and Google Scholar to identify 15 additional meaningful scene classes.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Experts in the field of remote sensing image interpretation from Northwestern Polytechnical University (NWPU).
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset enables the remote sensing community to develop and evaluate various data-driven algorithms for applications such as natural hazards detection, land use and land cover (LULC) determination, geospatial object detection, geographic image retrieval, vegetation mapping, environment monitoring, and urban planning.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: For four scene classes (island, lake, mountain, and snowberg), the spatial resolutions are lower than the typical 30 m to 0.2 m range of other classes. Relatively large confusions between visually similar classes may occur (e.g., 'church' vs 'palace', 'dense residential' vs 'medium residential', 'golf court' vs 'meadow') due to similar global structure, spatial layout, or dominant color.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for training, testing, and validation of remote sensing image scene classification methods, including handcrafted feature based methods, unsupervised feature learning based methods, and deep feature learning based methods (e.g., CNNs such as AlexNet, VGGNet-16, GoogLeNet). Recommended training-test ratios evaluated in the paper are 10%-90% and 20%-80%.
